status: Experimental development selection, frozen after initial extraction errors and before repair scoring; not a production recommendation
reason: At random 0.01% pixel damage, header errors were 0–4 bytes, payload errors reached 33 bytes, runs reached 4 bytes, and 255-byte regions reached 17 bad bytes. Compare payload parity16 (8-symbol radius) and parity32 (16-symbol radius), with fixed parity16 header. Compare whole-byte round-robin for parity16 because short bursts and unequal region counts can shift errors across shortened codewords. At larger damage, counts greatly exceed these radii and adaptive salt changes; keep these failures, not a stronger-salt workaround.
notSelected: No bit interleaver: observed multi-bit grouping within small byte runs makes dispersion into more erroneous symbols a risk without a demonstrated need. No parity64: adds cost while 512-byte admission already fails for parity32 and larger damage is dominated by salt/header failure. Identity and round-robin are identical when only one codeword is present; report that limitation.
